title: Build, test and contribution workflow
one_liner: You build with meson or configure, prove your change with regress, isolation and TAP tests, format with pgindent, then mail a patch to pgsql-hackers.
analogy: Like fixing a car part: build the car, run the test track, polish to the shop's style, then send your repair note to the mechanics' mailing list.
big_picture: The tree has two build systems: configure plus make (configure.ac, GNUmakefile.in) and meson (meson.build). Both build the same code.
Tests live in src/test (regress, isolation, recovery, ...), in contrib/*/ and in src/bin/*/t. "make check-world" runs most of them. TAP tests need --enable-tap-tests (meson: -Dtap_tests=enabled).
Regress tests compare real output to saved expected .out files. Any difference is a failure, written to regression.diffs.
pgindent reformats C code to one style. It uses pg_bsd_indent and src/tools/pgindent/typedefs.list.
Docs are DocBook files ending in .sgml in doc/src/sgml. A user-visible change needs a doc change in the same patch. Build with "make html" or "ninja docs".
Patches go by email to pgsql-hackers and are tracked in a Commitfest. Only committers push to the main repo.

flow.detail: Run 'meson setup build' then ninja. Or run ./configure then make. Use cassert and tap tests on while developing.
Follow the 4-column tab style and ereport rules for messages.
Add SQL in sql/, the expected result in expected/, and list it in parallel_schedule. Concurrency tests become specs.
make check, make check-world, or meson test. pg_regress writes regression.diffs on failure.
Run pgindent on your changed C files. Add new typedef names to typedefs.list first.
Edit the matching SGML file and check it builds with 'make html' in doc/src/sgml.
git format-patch gives a mailable patch. Send it to pgsql-hackers.
flow.where: postgresql.org/developer and the wiki page "Submitting a Patch"

flow.detail: Register it in a Commitfest. A committer pushes it, and may backpatch fixes to stable branches.

diagram.claim: A change moves from your editor through build, tests and formatting, then by email to a committer.

interview.q: What are the two ways to build PostgreSQL from this tree?
answer: Autoconf: ./configure then make, driven by configure.ac and GNUmakefile.in.
Meson: 'meson setup build' then ninja, driven by meson.build.
Both build the same source and run the same tests.
interview.trap: Meson is not a wrapper around configure. They are separate build systems that you must keep in sync.

interview.q: Which configure options help a developer?
answer: --enable-cassert turns on internal sanity checks (Assert).
--enable-tap-tests lets the Perl t/ tests run.
Meson equivalents are options like cassert and tap_tests in meson_options.txt.
interview.trap: Benchmarking with cassert on gives misleading, slow numbers.

interview.q: How does 'make check' differ from 'make installcheck'?
answer: check builds a temporary install and starts a throwaway server.
installcheck tests an already running installed server.
check-world runs every suite including contrib and src/bin.

interview.q: How does a regress test actually pass or fail?
answer: pg_regress runs each file in sql/ and writes results.
It diffs results against the file in expected/.
Any difference fails and is saved in regression.diffs.
interview.trap: A passing test does not mean correct output, only output that matches the saved file.

interview.q: I added a regress test. What files must I touch?
answer: Add sql/mytest.sql and expected/mytest.out.
List mytest in src/test/regress/parallel_schedule.
Check the .out is correct by reading it, not just copying it.

interview.q: When do you use isolation tests or TAP tests instead?
answer: Isolation specs in src/test/isolation/specs test several sessions interleaving.
TAP tests are Perl scripts in t/ directories, such as src/test/recovery/t.
They start whole servers, so use them for replication, recovery and command-line tools.
interview.trap: Plain regress cannot test concurrency, because it runs one session per file.

interview.q: What does pgindent do and what is typedefs.list for?
answer: pgindent reformats C code using pg_bsd_indent.
It needs to know type names, kept in src/tools/pgindent/typedefs.list.
Add your new typedefs there or spacing around them will be odd.
interview.trap: Do not reindent whole files you did not change; it makes the patch noisy.

interview.q: How does a patch travel from your laptop to the main repo?
answer: Make it with git format-patch and email it to pgsql-hackers.
Add it to a Commitfest so reviewers do not lose it.
Reviewers comment, you send a new version, then a committer pushes it.
Bug fixes may be backpatched to older stable branches.
interview.trap: Opening a GitHub pull request does nothing here. The project works by mailing list.

interview.q: What makes a good first patch?
answer: Small and focused: a doc fix, a clearer error message or a missing test.
Include tests and doc changes, and pass check-world.
Follow sources.sgml style and keep the diff clean.
Review someone else's patch in the Commitfest to learn the process.

contributor_tips: Start by reading doc/src/sgml/sources.sgml and src/tools/pgindent/README before touching C code.
Build with cassert and tap tests on, and run 'make check' often while you work.
A doc typo or missing test is a safe first patch; review a Commitfest patch to learn the review style.
Never reindent code you did not change, and never hand-edit expected .out files without understanding the diff.

glossary.meaning: Test driver that runs SQL and diffs output against expected files
Perl script test in a t/ directory that starts real servers
A file describing steps of several sessions to test concurrency
Tool that formats C code to the project style
Periodic review cycle that tracks submitted patches
Applying a fix to older stable release branches too

more: GitHub is a read-only mirror. Pull requests are not used.
Alternative expected files (foo_1.out) cover platform-specific output.
Run one test: make check-tests TESTS=name, or meson test with a suite.
Changing a system catalog needs a catversion bump.
Bug fixes can be backpatched to stable branches. Features cannot.
pg_bsd_indent must be on your PATH before pgindent works.
